subject: HearthHealth — Hosted API rate proposal and exec sign-off
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@hearthhealth.com>, HearthHealth Procurement <purchasing@hearthhealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API pricing for pilot - volume proposal

Hi Olivia / team,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — great product fit. Per our call, attached is a rate proposal and a conservative 24-month usage forecast built from the pilot metrics you shared. Short summary of the ask: HearthHealth is looking to commit to a 24-month hosted API contract with a ramp to ~600M tokens/month. To get to the unit economics you need, we have a proposed blended discount of 30% off list Hosted API usage rates in year one with planned step-downs.

I know >20% requires exec sign-off on our side; please consider this a formal request for that clearance. If helpful I can surface the ARR impact and references.

Attachments: HearthHealth_RateProposal_20261120.pdf (PDF, 120KB), hh_usage_forecast_20261119.xlsx (XLSX, 85KB)

Key asks from HearthHealth:
- 30% off Hosted API token pricing in year 1 (committed monthly minimums)
- 24-month term; auto-renew with 60-day notice
- Standard Redwood SLA; want clarification on throughput guarantees for burst traffic

Next steps: if you can confirm the commercial boundary (target effective rate and minimum committed spend), I will loop legal and request deal desk escalation here.

Thanks,
Rachel

From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@hearthhealth.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing for pilot - volume proposal

Thanks Rachel — got the proposal and forecast, appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple quick clarifying questions before we escalate internally:

1) The 30% target — is that net of any volume tiers/overage caps or the headline list discount? We need an apples-to-apples monthly effective rate.
2) Does that pricing assume access to any Dedicated features (reserved capacity) or is this purely Hosted API? We want to avoid surprises around throughput for our peak processing windows.
3) Are you able to provide a sample SLO language or a short playbook for how Redwood handles burst throttling?

We are aligned on timeline and would like to get this in front of procurement and legal next week. If you believe 30% is outside your standard approval band, please let me know and we can coordinate the ask to your execs.

Best,
Olivia Barnes
Head of Platform Integrations | HearthHealth
olivia@hearthhealth.com
